scenarios.title: One-off lake shock followed by recovery
scenarios.persona: You value long-term sustainability and fair access. You avoid overreacting to weak evidence.
scenarios.role: You are one of five fishers managing a shared lake. Decide your own harvest each round.
observations: Round 1: everyone harvests 10 from stock 100; after normal regeneration, stock returns to 100.
Round 2: everyone harvests 10 from stock 100; stock returns to 100.
Round 3: everyone harvests 10 from stock 100; stock returns to 100.
Round 4: everyone again harvests exactly 10, but an observed one-day contamination event kills fish and next stock is 78. The contamination is reported as cleared at the end of the round.
Round 5: all four partners harvest 8 and you previously harvested 8. Water tests are normal and regeneration returns to its earlier rate; stock recovery matches the original rule.
Round 6: all four partners harvest 10 and you previously harvested 10. Water remains normal and stock again follows the original regeneration rule.

scenarios.title: Own water need increases while market stays stable
scenarios.persona: You are budget-conscious, moderately risk-averse, and care about fair access to water.
scenarios.role: You participate in a daily water auction. Initial health is 8/10, daily need is 2 units, and initial budget is 600. Choose one bid each day.
observations: Day 1: supply is 10 and other bids are 45-55. Your need is 2, previous bid is 50, and you receive enough water.
Day 2: supply is 10 and other bids are 45-55. Your need remains 2 and a bid of 50 succeeds.
Day 3: supply is 10 and other bids are 45-55. Your need remains 2 and a bid of 50 succeeds.
Day 4: supply and other bids remain unchanged. A documented medical treatment raises your own daily need from 2 to 4 units for the next three days; your health is 5/10 and budget is 450.
Day 5: supply is 10 and other bids remain 45-55. Your treatment continues, need is 4, health is 6/10, and budget is 360.

scenarios.title: Public-project productivity falls while contributions remain stable
scenarios.persona: You value reciprocity, community welfare, and prudent use of your private endowment.
scenarios.role: Five residents each receive 20 tokens per round and choose a contribution to a public project.
observations: Round 1: everyone contributes 10. The project doubles the pool and each resident receives 20 back.
Round 2: everyone contributes 10. The project again doubles the pool.
Round 3: Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each contribute 10; you previously contributed 10. Returns remain normal.
Round 4: public ledgers show that all five contributions remain 10, but a documented equipment failure lowers the project multiplier and each resident receives only 12.
Round 5: all residents reduce contributions to 8. The same equipment failure persists and the multiplier remains low.

scenarios.title: One resident free-rides while project productivity stays stable
scenarios.persona: You value reciprocity, community welfare, and prudent use of your private endowment.
scenarios.role: Five residents each receive 20 tokens per round and choose a contribution to a public project.
observations: Round 1: everyone contributes 10. The project doubles the pool and each resident receives 20 back.
Round 2: everyone contributes 10. The project again doubles the pool.
Round 3: everyone contributes 10 and returns remain normal.
Round 4: Alice, Bob, Carol, and you contribute 10, but the public ledger shows David contributes 0. The project multiplier remains exactly two, and each resident receives only 16.
Round 5: David again contributes 0 after promising 10; the other four residents remain at 10 and the multiplier remains two.

scenarios.title: One representative repeatedly violates precautions
scenarios.persona: You value public health, proportional restrictions, and fair treatment of neighbors.
scenarios.role: You are one of five neighborhood representatives choosing a daily precaution effort from 0 to 10.
observations: Day 1: all representatives choose precaution 5. New infections remain at 5.
Day 2: everyone again chooses 5 and infections remain at 5.
Day 3: everyone chooses 5; pathogen sequencing and transmission conditions remain stable.

Day 4: Alice, Bob, Carol, and you maintain precaution 5. David publicly reports 5 but verified mobility logs show he holds a crowded event; infections rise to 14 while pathogen properties remain unchanged.
Day 5: David holds another crowded event; all other representatives maintain their policy and laboratory estimates of transmissibility remain stable.

scenarios.title: Bob increases consumption while generation stays stable
scenarios.persona: You value reliable electricity, conservation, and equitable burden sharing.
scenarios.role: Five households share a solar microgrid. Choose your consumption from 0 to 10 units each evening.
observations: Evening 1: generation is 30 and every household consumes 5. The battery ends at 20.
Evening 2: generation is 30 and all consume 5. Battery remains healthy.
Evening 3: generation is 30 and all consume 5.
Evening 4: generation remains 30. Alice, Carol, David, and you consume 5, but Bob's verified smart meter records 23; the battery falls by the same amount as in a severe generation shortfall.
Evening 5: generation remains 30 and Bob again consumes 18 after agreeing to 4; all other households comply with 4.

scenarios.title: A lane closure increases travel time under stable driver behavior
scenarios.persona: You value predictable travel, courtesy, and avoiding unnecessary congestion for others.
scenarios.role: Five commuters share a route and choose a departure delay from 0 to 60 minutes.
observations: Day 1: all commuters depart at the usual time and travel takes 25 minutes.
Day 2: departure patterns are unchanged and travel takes 25 minutes.
Day 3: all five follow the agreed schedule and travel remains 25 minutes.
Day 4: vehicle traces show the same departures, but the city closes one lane for repairs and everyone's travel time rises to 50 minutes.
Day 5: the closure remains posted. Other commuters stagger departure by 15 minutes.
